# Tellurium

**Faster chunk generation for Minecraft that produces the same world.** The GPU part runs on Vulkan (no CUDA). Without a suitable GPU, or for any world generator that has not been tested, chunks are generated by vanilla code.

> The mod id, jar names, commands and config file still use the name `worldgennext`.

## Features

- **Terrain and surface on the GPU** for the tested world generators: vanilla Overworld, Nether and End, Terralith, Tectonic, Terralith with Tectonic, and Incendium. Terrain only for Amplified Nether and Nullscape. Any other generator, and any chunk the GPU marks as unsafe, uses vanilla code.
- **Structure, carver and feature steps run in parallel.** The hottest vanilla loops (ore veins, biome lookups) are replaced with cheaper versions that give the same results.
- **Background saving**: chunks are encoded and compressed off the server thread.
- **Built-in pregenerator**: `/worldgennext pregen start <radius>`.
- **Works with Chunky, Distant Horizons and Voxy** (details below).

## Throughput

Chunks per second, generated to FULL and saved. Reference host: 24 logical cores, RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GB heap, ScalableLux.

| World generator | Vanilla | Tellurium |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vanilla Overworld | 124 | 2,620–2,860 |
| Tectonic | 90–105 | 2,702–2,790 |
| Terralith | 41–48 | 1,750–1,810 |
| Terralith + Tectonic | 56–62 | 2,019–2,042 |

The same Chunky pregeneration (vanilla world, 35,721 / 142,129 chunks) on the same server with other chunk generation mods:

| | chunks/s |
| --- | --- |
| Vanilla | 127 |
| C2ME | 930 / 1,064 |
| C2ME + OpenCL module | 2,020–2,070 / 2,140 |
| **Tellurium** | **2,960–2,970 / 3,479** |

From a cold start with default settings, the built-in pregenerator generated 251,001 chunks in 74 s (3,378 chunks/s, one run). Every saved chunk read back without errors.

## "The same world"

These checks compare Tellurium with vanilla generating one chunk at a time, with every optimization turned off:

- **Through the SURFACE step**, per-chunk digests (blocks, heightmaps, biomes, structure starts and references, post-processing marks) match in all 15 test contexts, 8,281 chunks each: three vanilla Overworld seeds, the Nether, the End, seven biome-specific Overworld areas, Terralith, Tectonic and the two together.
- **Through CARVERS**, the same digests match in the contexts re-run after each change.
- **From FEATURES on**, vanilla itself is not reproducible from run to run, so each piece is checked separately against vanilla: the ore-vein scan (871,121 veins, no difference), the biome shortcut (6.8 million lookups, no difference), and saved chunks reread after reopening the world.

## Requirements

- **Minecraft 1.21.1** with NeoForge 21.1.176+ or Fabric (loader 0.16+ and Fabric API). Builds also exist for **1.21.11** (NeoForge 21.11.45+ / Fabric), **1.21.8** (NeoForge 21.8.54+ / Fabric) and **1.21.4** (Fabric).
- Java 21.
- For the GPU part, a GPU with Vulkan and 64-bit float support. Without one, the mod logs why and still applies the CPU-side improvements.
- Recommended: **ScalableLux**. Lighting is not handled by this mod, and all figures above were measured with ScalableLux installed.

Install it on a dedicated server, or on the client for singleplayer. A multiplayer server only needs the mod on the server.

On 1.21.11, the tested list covers vanilla, Terralith, Tectonic and the two together. On 1.21.4 and 1.21.8, it covers vanilla and Terralith, and Tectonic uses vanilla code. Everything else on this page was measured on 1.21.1.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/worldgennext status` | Shows the GPU and what each dimension is generated with (and why), plus chunk counts and tips |
| `/worldgennext pregen start <radius>` | Generates a square `radius` chunks in each direction from where you stand (from the console: around the world spawn) |
| `/worldgennext pregen start <radius> <x> <z>` | The same, centred on block coordinates |
| `/worldgennext pregen start worldborder` | Generates everything inside the world border |
| `/worldgennext pregen pause` / `resume` / `stop` / `status` | `resume` also continues a job that a restart interrupted |

In singleplayer, the world's owner can use the commands without cheats enabled. To pregenerate another dimension, run e.g. `/execute in minecraft:the_nether run worldgennext pregen start 100`.

## Configuration

`config/worldgennext.toml` is written on first start:

```toml
enabled = true            # false: behave exactly as without the mod

[gpu]
mode = "auto"             # "auto" | "check" | "force" (untested generators too) | "off"

[generation]
parallel_steps = true

[saving]
async = true
compression_level = 1     # 1 fastest (files ~12% larger) ... 6 = vanilla size ... 9

[pregen]
in_flight = 1024
progress_seconds = 10
```

**World generators that are not on the tested list** (datapacks, other terrain mods) use vanilla code by default. To find out whether the GPU reproduces one exactly, set `gpu.mode = "check"`, generate a few thousand chunks across different biomes and look at `/worldgennext status`, which counts the chunks compared and the chunks that differed. If none differ, `gpu.mode = "force"` turns the GPU on for that world. This is evidence for the chunks you checked, not proof for all chunks.

## Other mods

- **Chunky**: works. By default Chunky requests 50 chunks at a time, which limits any generator to about 1,000 chunks/s, so when Chunky is installed Tellurium raises that limit. Set `pregen.tune_chunky = false` to keep Chunky's setting.
- **Distant Horizons**: Distant Horizons still makes its rough pass for far terrain. When it refines those chunks, Tellurium generates them. A dedicated server built full-detail distant terrain about 4.6× as fast as with Distant Horizons alone.
- **Voxy**: in singleplayer, or on the host of a LAN world, Tellurium generates the terrain within 128 chunks of each player and passes it to Voxy. On the reference host that was 73,984 chunks in about 40 s.
- **Also run with this mod, all working:** Biomes O' Plenty, Oh The Biomes We've Gone, Nature's Spirit, Geophilic, William Wythers' Overhauled Overworld, nine YUNG's structure mods, Dungeons and Taverns, When Dungeons Arise, Structory, Regions Unexplored, Incendium, Amplified Nether, Nullscape and Lithium. Where the GPU handles a mod's terrain, it matched vanilla on every chunk compared. Where it can't, that world uses vanilla code.

## Not tested

Linux, GPUs other than an RTX 5070 Ti, world generators outside the tested list, other mods that change chunk generation or saving, and LAN play.

If the graphics driver resets, the mod reports it once in the log and in `/worldgennext status`, then generates on the CPU until the next restart. Chunks already generated are not affected.
